google_compute_region_backend_service.ou.text: Settings controlling the eviction of unhealthy hosts from the load balancing pool for the backend service. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

A Duration represents a fixed-length span of time represented as a count of seconds and fractions of seconds at nanosecond resolution. It is independent of any calendar and concepts like "day" or "month". Range is approximately 10,000 years. Optional.

Span of time that's a fraction of a second at nanosecond resolution. Durations less than one second are represented with a 0 `seconds` field and a positive `nanos` field. Must be from 0 to 999,999,999 inclusive. Optional.

Span of time at a resolution of a second. Must be from 0 to 315,576,000,000 inclusive. Note: these bounds are computed from: 60 sec/min * 60 min/hr * 24 hr/day * 365.25 days/year * 10000 years Optional.

Number of consecutive errors before a backend endpoint is ejected from the load balancing pool. When the backend endpoint is accessed over HTTP, a 5xx return code qualifies as an error. Defaults to 5. Optional.

The number of consecutive gateway failures (502, 503, 504 status or connection errors that are mapped to one of those status codes) before a consecutive gateway failure ejection occurs. Defaults to 3. Optional.

The percentage chance that a backend endpoint will be ejected when an outlier status is detected through consecutive 5xx. This setting can be used to disable ejection or to ramp it up slowly. Defaults to 0. Optional.

The percentage chance that a backend endpoint will be ejected when an outlier status is detected through consecutive gateway failures. This setting can be used to disable ejection or to ramp it up slowly. Defaults to 100. Optional.

The percentage chance that a backend endpoint will be ejected when an outlier status is detected through success rate statistics. This setting can be used to disable ejection or to ramp it up slowly. Defaults to 100. Not supported when the backend service uses Serverless NEG. Optional.

A Duration represents a fixed-length span of time represented as a count of seconds and fractions of seconds at nanosecond resolution. It is independent of any calendar and concepts like "day" or "month". Range is approximately 10,000 years. Optional.

Span of time that's a fraction of a second at nanosecond resolution. Durations less than one second are represented with a 0 `seconds` field and a positive `nanos` field. Must be from 0 to 999,999,999 inclusive. Optional.

Span of time at a resolution of a second. Must be from 0 to 315,576,000,000 inclusive. Note: these bounds are computed from: 60 sec/min * 60 min/hr * 24 hr/day * 365.25 days/year * 10000 years Optional.
Maximum percentage of backend endpoints in the load balancing pool for the backend service that can be ejected if the ejection conditions are met. Defaults to 50%. Optional.

The number of backend endpoints in the load balancing pool that must have enough request volume to detect success rate outliers. If the number of backend endpoints is fewer than this setting, outlier detection via success rate statistics is not performed for any backend endpoint in the load balancing pool. Defaults to 5. Not supported when the backend service uses Serverless NEG. Optional.

The minimum number of total requests that must be collected in one interval (as defined by the interval duration above) to include this backend endpoint in success rate based outlier detection. If the volume is lower than this setting, outlier detection via success rate statistics is not performed for that backend endpoint. Defaults to 100. Not supported when the backend service uses Serverless NEG. Optional.

This factor is used to determine the ejection threshold for success rate outlier ejection. The ejection threshold is the difference between the mean success rate, and the product of this factor and the standard deviation of the mean success rate: mean - (stdev * successRateStdevFactor). This factor is divided by a thousand to get a double. That is, if the desired factor is 1.9, the runtime value should be 1900. Defaults to 1900. Not supported when the backend service uses Serverless NEG. Optional.

google_compute_region_backend_service.pa.text: Additional Backend Service parameters. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

Tag keys/values directly bound to this resource. Tag keys and values have the same definition as resource manager tags. The field is allowed for INSERT only. The keys/values to set on the resource should be specified in either ID { : } or Namespaced format { : }. google_compute_region_security_policy.ad.text: Configuration options for Cloud Armor Adaptive Protection (CAAP). Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

If set to true, enables CAAP for L7 DDoS detection. This field is only supported in Global Security Policies of type CLOUD_ARMOR. Optional.
Rule visibility can be one of the following: STANDARD - opaque rules. (default) PREMIUM - transparent rules. This field is only supported in Global Security Policies of type CLOUD_ARMOR. Optional.
Configuration options for layer7 adaptive protection for various customizable thresholds. Optional.
The confidence threshold percentage that triggers auto-deployment of adaptive protection. Must be a number between 0 and 100.
Duration in seconds after which the auto-deployed adaptive protection mitigation expires. This sets how long the mitigation remains active before being automatically withdrawn.

Threshold for the ratio of impacted baseline traffic that triggers automatic deployment of the DDoS defense. When the measured impacted baseline exceeds this value, the adaptive protection automatically deploys the defense.
The load threshold in requests per second per backend instance that triggers automatic deployment of Layer 7 adaptive protection.

The absolute QPS threshold (in requests per second) that triggers adaptive protection detection. When traffic to the protected resource exceeds this rate, the system may consider it anomalous and apply DDoS defense actions.
The minimum number of requests per second that triggers adaptive protection detection for this threshold configuration.

Detection threshold relative to the baseline queries per second (QPS). A value of 1.0 means the threshold equals the baseline QPS; values greater than 1.0 require proportionally more traffic to trigger detection.
A unique name for this threshold configuration, used to identify it within the layer 7 DDoS defense settings of the adaptive protection config.

A list of traffic granularity configurations for a layer 7 DDoS defense threshold. These configs define how traffic is aggregated or segmented (e.g., by source IP or range) when determining whether a threshold is exceeded, enabling granular control over adaptive protection rules.

When set to true, traffic is tracked separately for each unique value of the configured traffic granularity type (e.g., each unique HTTP header host). When false, traffic is aggregated according to the granularity type.

The type of traffic granularity to use for the layer 7 DDoS defense threshold. This can be HTTP_HEADER_HOST to group traffic by host header, HTTP_PATH to group by request path, or UNSPECIFIED_TYPE if not set.
The IP address or CIDR range for this traffic granularity configuration. The interpretation depends on the associated type field (IP or CIDR).
Custom configuration for JSON parsing, used in the advanced options of a security policy. It typically specifies content types that should be parsed as JSON.

A list of custom Content-Type header values to apply the JSON parsing. google_compute_region_security_policy.cr.text: Output only. [Output Only] Creation timestamp inRFC3339 text format. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_region_security_policy.dd.text: The mode of DDoS adaptive protection for this region security policy. Set to DISABLED to turn it off, ENABLED to turn it on, or PREVIEW to test without enforcing. The UNSPECIFIED values are placeholders for internal use.

DDoS Protection for Network Load Balancers (and VMs with public IPs) builds DDoS mitigations that minimize collateral damage. It quantifies this as the fraction of a non-abuse baseline that's inadvertently blocked. Rules whose collateral damage exceeds ddosImpactedBaselineThreshold will not be deployed. Using a lower value will prioritize keeping collateral damage low, possibly at the cost of its effectiveness in rate limiting some or all of the attack. It should typically be unset, so Advanced DDoS (and Adaptive Protection) uses the best mitigation it can find. Setting the threshold is advised if there are logs for false positive detections with high collateral damage, and will cause Advanced DDoS to attempt to find a less aggressive rule that satisfies the constraint. If a suitable rule cannot be found, the system falls back to either no mitigation for smaller attacks or broader network throttles for larger ones. Optional.
The DDoS protection tier to use for the regional security policy. Valid values are STANDARD, ADVANCED, and ADVANCED_PREVIEW.

google_compute_region_security_policy.ru.text: A list of rules that belong to this policy. There must always be a default rule which is a rule with priority 2147483647 and match all condition (for the match condition this means match "*" for srcIpRanges and for the networkMatch condition every field must be either match "*" or not set). If no rules are provided when creating a security policy, a default rule with action "allow" will be added. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The action to perform when a request matches the rule. Allowed values are 'allow' or 'deny', with an optional custom HTTP status code for deny (e.g., 'deny(403)').
An optional description of the security policy rule.
Specifies the header action to apply to requests that match this rule. This block allows you to add or remove HTTP headers using request_headers_to_adds and request_headers_to_remove.
A list of request headers to add to the request. Each element in the list contains a header_name and header_value.
The name of the HTTP request header to add to the request. For example, 'X-Forwarded-For'.
The value of the custom header to be added to requests.
The kind of the resource, set to 'compute#securityPolicyRule' for a region security policy rule.
The match criteria for this security policy rule. It defines the conditions under which the rule is applied, such as source IP ranges, ports, or request expressions.
The configuration for the match condition, specifying the source and destination IP ranges to match.
A list of source IP address ranges in CIDR format. The rule matches requests whose source IP address falls within any of these ranges.
The expr block provides a Common Expression Language (CEL) expression that defines the matching condition for the security policy rule. The rule is applied when the expression evaluates to true.
The Common Expression Language (CEL) expression that defines the criteria for matching this security policy rule.
The source location of the expression, used for debugging. This may specify a file name, line number, or other identifier of where the expression was defined.
A short, human-readable title for the expression. This is optional and helps identify the purpose or meaning of the match expression.
Options for the expression in the match rule, such as reCAPTCHA configuration.
A list of reCAPTCHA Enterprise site keys used for action tokens. These keys are used to validate the action token in the request.
A list of site keys used to verify reCAPTCHA session tokens.
The versioned expression for the match rule. Must be set to SRC_IPS_V1 when using source IP-based matching; this is the only supported value.
The network match configuration for the rule, specifying network conditions like source IP ranges, source region codes, and user-defined fields that the request must satisfy for the rule to apply.
Destination IP address ranges in CIDR format for matching network traffic.
A list of destination ports to match, where each entry is a single port (e.g., '80') or a range (e.g., '80-90'). Used in L4 network match conditions for security policy rules.
A list of source Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) to match. The rule applies to requests originating from networks belonging to any of the specified ASNs.
A list of source IP address ranges (CIDR format) that the rule matches for incoming traffic.
A list of source ports to match for this rule. Each entry can be a single port number or a port range (e.g., '80' or '80-90'). If unspecified, all source ports are matched.
A list of source region codes to match against the source region of the traffic.
A list of user-defined field configurations used to match network traffic within a security policy rule. Each configuration specifies a field name and a list of values to match against.
The name of the user-defined field to match in the request. This corresponds to the field name as defined in the security policy's user-defined fields.
A list of values to match the user-defined field against. The incoming packet matches if the field value equals any of the specified values.

The preconfigured_waf_config block configures settings for the preconfigured WAF rules applied to this security policy rule. It allows you to customize the inspection behavior, such as defining exclusions to skip certain parts of requests from WAF evaluation.

A list of exclusion rules for this preconfigured WAF rule, specifying request attributes (e.g., headers, cookies, query parameters) that should be ignored during WAF evaluation to avoid false positives or allow specific traffic.
A list of request cookies to exclude from WAF evaluation. Each exclusion specifies an operator (EQUALS or STARTS_WITH) and a value representing the cookie name to match.
The operator to apply when matching the request cookie value. Allowed values are CONTAINS, ENDS_WITH, EQUALS, EQUALS_ANY, STARTS_WITH.

The value of the request cookie to exclude from WAF evaluation. When specified, only cookies whose value exactly matches this field are excluded; when omitted, the exclusion applies to any cookie with the matching key.

A list of request headers to exclude from the preconfigured WAF rule evaluation. Each object specifies a header key, a match operator, and a value; the operator can be one of EQUALS_TO, EQUALS_ANY, STARTS_WITH, ENDS_WITH, or CONTAINS.
The operator to apply when matching the request header. Valid values are: CONTAINS, ENDS_WITH, EQUALS, EQUALS_ANY, STARTS_WITH.
A list of query parameters to exclude from WAF evaluation, allowing specific query parameters to be ignored by preconfigured WAF rules.
The operator used to match the query parameter in the exclusion rule. Valid values are `CONTAINS`, `ENDS_WITH`, `EQUALS`, `EQUALS_ANY`, and `STARTS_WITH`.

The value of the query parameter to exclude from WAF evaluation. If a request query parameter matches this value, the parameter (or key-value pair) is excluded from the preconfigured WAF rule evaluation.
A list of request URIs to exclude from the preconfigured WAF rule evaluation. Each object specifies a URI matching condition, typically including a value and an operator.
The operator used to match the request URI. Allowed values are: CONTAINS, ENDS_WITH, EQUALS, EQUALS_ANY, STARTS_WITH.
The URI value to be excluded from the preconfigured WAF rule evaluation.
List of target rule IDs for the exclusion. When empty, all preconfigured WAF rules are excluded.
The target WAF rule set to which the exclusion applies.
Whether the rule is in preview mode. Preview rules are not enforced, but their actions are still logged and can be used to test rule behavior before enabling enforcement.
An integer that specifies the evaluation priority of the rule. Lower values are evaluated first. Must be unique within the security policy.
The duration in seconds that a client is banned after exceeding the ban threshold. Only applicable when exceed_action is set to 'ban'.
Threshold that, when exceeded, triggers banning of clients. This nested block is part of rate limit options; when a client surpasses the specified count within the interval, the client is banned.
The number of requests that must be exceeded within the configured interval to trigger a ban. Used in the ban_threshold of rate limiting for a security policy rule.
The time interval, in seconds, over which the ban threshold count is measured before a ban is enforced.
The action to take when a request is within the allowed rate limit. For rate limiting, this must be set to 'allow'.

Specifies the key type used to identify requests for rate limiting enforcement. Accepted values are: ALL, ASN, HTTP_COOKIE, HTTP_HEADER, HTTP_PATH, IP, REGION_CODE, SNI, TLS_JA3_FINGERPRINT, TLS_JA4_FINGERPRINT, USER_IP, and XFF_IP.
Specifies a list of key configurations used to enforce the rate limit. Each configuration contains the key type (e.g., IP, HTTP_HEADER) and an optional key name.
The name of the key (e.g., HTTP header or cookie name) to enforce rate limiting on. Required when enforce_on_key_type is HTTP_HEADER or COOKIE.

The type of key on which to enforce rate limiting. This specifies which request attribute (e.g., source IP, HTTP header, path) is used to identify and group clients for rate limiting. Valid values are: ALL, ASN, HTTP_COOKIE, HTTP_HEADER, HTTP_PATH, IP, REGION_CODE, SNI, TLS_JA3_FINGERPRINT, TLS_JA4_FINGERPRINT, USER_IP, XFF_IP.
The name of the header or cookie to enforce the rate limit on. This field is required when enforce_on_key is set to HTTP_HEADER or HTTP_COOKIE.
The action to take when a request exceeds the rate limit defined in these rate limit options.
Specifies the redirect action for requests that exceed the configured rate limit. This object defines the redirect type (e.g., EXTERNAL_302) and the target URL to redirect excess traffic to.
The URL to which requests that exceed the rate limit are redirected. This is used when the redirect type is set to EXTERNAL_302.
The type of redirect action to take when the rate limit is exceeded. Allowed values are EXTERNAL_302 and GOOGLE_RECAPTCHA.

Configuration for the rate limit threshold, specifying the maximum number of requests allowed within a given time interval before triggering the configured action. Typically includes fields like count and interval.
The number of requests allowed within the specified time interval before the rate limit action is enforced.
The interval in seconds over which the rate limit count is enforced.
The target URL to redirect to when the redirect type is EXTERNAL_302. Only set this when the redirect type is EXTERNAL_302.

The type of redirect to apply. If set to EXTERNAL_302, the request is redirected to the specified external target with a 302 status. If set to GOOGLE_RECAPTCHA, the request is redirected to a Google reCAPTCHA page.

google_compute_region_security_policy.ty.text: The type indicates the intended use of the security policy. - CLOUD_ARMOR: Cloud Armor backend security policies can be configured to filter incoming HTTP requests targeting backend services. They filter requests before they hit the origin servers. - CLOUD_ARMOR_EDGE: Cloud Armor edge security policies can be configured to filter incoming HTTP requests targeting backend services (including Cloud CDN-enabled) as well as backend buckets (Cloud Storage). They filter requests before the request is served from Google's cache. - CLOUD_ARMOR_INTERNAL_SERVICE (preview only): Cloud Armor internal service policies can be configured to filter HTTP requests targeting services managed by Traffic Director in a service mesh. They filter requests before the request is served from the application. - CLOUD_ARMOR_NETWORK: Cloud Armor network policies can be configured to filter packets targeting network load balancing resources such as backend services, target pools, target instances, and instances with external IPs. They filter requests before the request is served from the application. This field can be set only at resource creation time. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

A user-defined field consists of up to 4 bytes extracted from a fixed offset in the packet, relative to the IPv4, IPv6, TCP, or UDP header, with an optional mask to select certain bits. Rules may then specify matching values for these fields. Example: userDefinedFields: - name: "ipv4_fragment_offset" base: IPV4 offset: 6 size: 2 mask: "0x1fff" Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The base protocol or address family that the user-defined field applies to. Valid values are IPV4, IPV6, TCP, UDP.

A string representation of the bitmask used to extract the user-defined field from the network packet. The mask is applied to the field specified by the base, offset, and size to select the relevant bits for matching.
The byte offset from the specified base (e.g., IP header) where the user-defined field begins. Used together with `base` and `size` to define a custom packet field for matching.
The size of the user-defined field in bytes, which specifies how many bytes of the named field to inspect.

Specifies whether TLS 1.3 0-RTT Data ("Early Data") should be accepted for this service. Early Data allows a TLS resumption handshake to include the initial application payload (a HTTP request) alongside the handshake, reducing the effective round trips to "zero". This applies to TLS 1.3 connections over TCP (HTTP/2) as well as over UDP (QUIC/h3). This can improve application performance, especially on networks where interruptions may be common, such as on mobile. Requests with Early Data will have the "Early-Data" HTTP header set on the request, with a value of "1", to allow the backend to determine whether Early Data was included. Note: TLS Early Data may allow requests to be replayed, as the data is sent to the backend before the handshake has fully completed. Applications that allow idempotent HTTP methods to make non-idempotent changes, such as a GET request updating a database, should not accept Early Data on those requests, and reject requests with the "Early-Data: 1" HTTP header by returning a HTTP 425 (Too Early) status code, in order to remain RFC compliant. The default value is DISABLED. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_region_url_map.default_cu.text: Specifies the custom error response policy that must be applied when the backend service or backend bucket responds with an error. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

Specifies rules for returning error responses. In a given policy, if you specify rules for both a range of error codes as well as rules for specific error codes then rules with specific error codes have a higher priority. For example, assume that you configure a rule for 401 (Un-authorized) code, and another for all 4 series error codes (4XX). If the backend service returns a401, then the rule for 401 will be applied. However if the backend service returns a 403, the rule for4xx takes effect. Optional.

A list of HTTP status codes that this error response rule matches. When a backend returns one of these response codes, the custom error response is used. For example, "404" or "500". Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

The HTTP status code that the URL Map should return to the client when the error occurs. The value must be between 100 and 599. If not specified, the original error code is returned. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

The path to the custom error page for this error response rule. This is typically a relative URL path (e.g., '/custom-error.html') that serves the error response from the backend or a static content bucket. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

The full or partial URL to the BackendBucket resource that contains the custom error content. Examples are: - https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/project/global/backendBuckets/myBackendBucket - compute/v1/projects/project/global/backendBuckets/myBackendBucket - global/backendBuckets/myBackendBucket If errorService is not specified at lower levels likepathMatcher, pathRule and routeRule, an errorService specified at a higher level in theUrlMap will be used. IfUrlMap.defaultCustomErrorResponsePolicy contains one or moreerrorResponseRules[], it must specifyerrorService. If load balancer cannot reach the backendBucket, a simple Not Found Error will be returned, with the original response code (oroverrideResponseCode if configured). errorService is not supported for internal or regionalHTTP/HTTPS load balancers. Optional.

Negative caching allows per-status code TTLs to be set, in order to apply fine-grained caching for common errors or redirects. This can reduce the load on your origin and improve end-user experience by reducing response latency. When the `cacheMode` is set to `CACHE_ALL_STATIC` or `USE_ORIGIN_HEADERS`, negative caching applies to responses with the specified response code that lack any Cache-Control, Expires, or Pragma: no-cache directives. When the `cacheMode` is set to `FORCE_CACHE_ALL`, negative caching applies to all responses with the specified response code, and overrides any caching headers. By default, Cloud CDN applies the following TTLs to these HTTP status codes: * 300 (Multiple Choice), 301, 308 (Permanent Redirects): 10m * 404 (Not Found), 410 (Gone), 451 (Unavailable For Legal Reasons): 120s * 405 (Method Not Found), 501 (Not Implemented): 60s These defaults can be overridden in `negativeCachingPolicy`. If not specified, Cloud CDN applies negative caching by default. Optional.

Sets a cache TTL for the specified HTTP status code. `negativeCaching` must be enabled to configure `negativeCachingPolicy`. Omitting the policy and leaving `negativeCaching` enabled will use Cloud CDN's default cache TTLs. Note that when specifying an explicit `negativeCachingPolicy`, you should take care to specify a cache TTL for all response codes that you wish to cache. Cloud CDN will not apply any default negative caching when a policy exists. Optional.
HTTP status code for which the negative caching policy applies. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The duration for which a negative cache entry is retained. This is a Duration object containing 'seconds' and 'nanos' fields. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The nanosecond portion of the TTL duration. Must be an integer between 0 and 999,999,999 inclusive. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The number of seconds for the negative caching policy's TTL (time-to-live) duration, expressed as a string. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
If true then Cloud CDN will combine multiple concurrent cache fill requests into a small number of requests to the origin. If not specified, Cloud CDN applies request coalescing by default. Optional.

Specifies one or more conditions when this retry policy applies. Valid values are: - 5xx: retry is attempted if the instance or endpoint responds with any 5xx response code, or if the instance or endpoint does not respond at all. For example, disconnects, reset, read timeout, connection failure, and refused streams. - gateway-error: Similar to 5xx, but only applies to response codes 502, 503 or504. - connect-failure: a retry is attempted on failures connecting to the instance or endpoint. For example, connection timeouts. - retriable-4xx: a retry is attempted if the instance or endpoint responds with a 4xx response code. The only error that you can retry is error code 409. - refused-stream: a retry is attempted if the instance or endpoint resets the stream with a REFUSED_STREAM error code. This reset type indicates that it is safe to retry. - cancelled: a retry is attempted if the gRPC status code in the response header is set to cancelled. - deadline-exceeded: a retry is attempted if the gRPC status code in the response header is set todeadline-exceeded. - internal: a retry is attempted if the gRPC status code in the response header is set tointernal. - resource-exhausted: a retry is attempted if the gRPC status code in the response header is set toresource-exhausted. - unavailable: a retry is attempted if the gRPC status code in the response header is set tounavailable. Only the following codes are supported when the URL map is bound to target gRPC proxy that has validateForProxyless field set to true. - cancelled - deadline-exceeded - internal - resource-exhausted - unavailable Optional.

google_compute_router.bgp_peers.bfd.text: Configures Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) settings for this BGP peer. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.bgp_peers.bfd.min_.text: The minimum interval, in milliseconds, between received BFD control packets for this BGP peer. This setting controls how quickly the router detects a peer failure. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The minimum interval (in milliseconds) between BFD transmissions for this BGP peer. The value must be between 100 and 30000 milliseconds. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.bgp_peers.bfd.mult.text: The number of consecutive BFD control packets that must be missed before BFD declares the peer down. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.bgp_peers.bfd.sess.text: The BFD session initialization mode. Valid values are ACTIVE, DISABLED, and PASSIVE. ACTIVE initiates the BFD session, PASSIVE waits for the peer to initiate, and DISABLED disables BFD. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.bgp_peers.custom_l.text: A list of custom learned route IP address ranges for this BGP peer. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The IP range in CIDR notation to use as a custom learned IP range for the BGP peer. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
User-specified priority for routes learned from this BGP peer. Must be between 0 and 65535 inclusive, defaults to 100. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.bgp_peers.enable.text: Indicates whether the BGP peer is enabled. The allowed values are TRUE and FALSE. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.bgp_peers.enable_i.text: Enables IPv4 on the BGP peer. This flag is set to true by default. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
Enables IPv6 for the BGP peer. Set to true to allow the BGP peer to exchange IPv6 routes. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.bgp_peers.export_p.text: List of names of Cloud Router route policies to apply to outgoing routes advertised to this BGP peer. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.bgp_peers.import_p.text: A list of Cloud Router route policy names that this BGP peer applies to incoming routes. These policies control which routes are accepted from the BGP peer. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.bgp_peers.interfac.text: The name of the router interface the BGP peer is associated with. This must match the name of an existing interface on the same Compute Router. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.bgp_peers.ipv4_nex.text: The IPv4 address that this BGP peer uses as the next hop for advertised routes. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.bgp_peers.ipv6_nex.text: The IPv6 address used as the next-hop for routes advertised to this BGP peer. If not specified, the default IPv6 next-hop (typically the interface's address) is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.bgp_peers.manageme.text: The management type of the BGP peer, which indicates whether the peer is managed by the associated attachment or by the user. Valid values are 'MANAGED_BY_ATTACHMENT' and 'MANAGED_BY_USER'. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.bgp_peers.md5_auth.text: The name of the MD5 authentication key to use for this BGP peer. The key must be defined in the router's BGP configuration. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.bgp_peers.peer_asn.text: The autonomous system number (ASN) of the BGP peer. Required when configuring a BGP peer on a Compute Router. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.bgp_peers.peer_ip_.text: The IP address of the BGP peer that this router will establish a BGP session with. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.bgp_peers.peer_ipv.text: The IPv4 address of the BGP peer, used as the next hop for routes learned from this peer. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.bgp_peers.router_a.text: The URI of the VM instance that is the router appliance for this BGP peer. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.creation_timestamp.text: Output only. [Output Only] Creation timestamp inRFC3339 text format. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.description.text: An optional description of this resource. Provide this property when you create the resource. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.encrypted_intercon.text: Indicates if a router is dedicated for use with encrypted VLAN attachments (interconnectAttachments). Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.id.text: [Output Only] The unique identifier for the resource. This identifier is defined by the server. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.interfaces.text: Router interfaces. To create a BGP peer that uses a router interface, the interface must have one of the following fields specified: - linkedVpnTunnel - linkedInterconnectAttachment - subnetwork You can create a router interface without any of these fields specified. However, you cannot create a BGP peer that uses that interface. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.interfaces.ip_rang.text: The IP address and range for the router interface, used for BGP sessions. This can be a single IP address or a CIDR range in the form of 'IP/30'. If not specified, GCP will assign an IP address automatically. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.interfaces.ip_vers.text: The IP version used by this interface. Valid values are IPV4 and IPV6. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.interfaces.linked_.text: The URL of the interconnect attachment to link with this router interface. This is used when the interface is for a VLAN attachment on an Interconnect. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The name of the VPN tunnel that this interface is linked to. Use this when the interface is of type 'tunnel'. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.interfaces.managem.text: Indicates who manages this interface: MANAGED_BY_ATTACHMENT means the interface is managed by a VLAN attachment (Cloud Interconnect), while MANAGED_BY_USER means it is configured by the user. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.interfaces.private.text: The private IP address of the Compute Router interface. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.interfaces.redunda.text: The name of another interface in the same router that serves as the redundancy pair for this interface. When set, this interface is configured as part of a redundant BGP session. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.interfaces.subnetw.text: The name or self-link of the subnetwork to which this router interface is attached. This field is used when the interface is associated with a subnetwork, such as for router appliance interfaces. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.kind.text: Output only. [Output Only] Type of resource. Always compute#router for routers. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.md5_authentication.text: Keys used for MD5 authentication. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The shared secret key used for MD5 authentication in the BGP session. This value is provided to the peer to authenticate the router. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The name of the MD5 authentication key. It uniquely identifies the key within the router's BGP configuration. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.name.text: Name of the resource. Provided by the client when the resource is created. The name must be 1-63 characters long, and comply withRFC1035. Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters long and match the regular expression `[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?` which means the first character must be a lowercase letter, and all following characters must be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit, except the last character, which cannot be a dash. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.text: A list of NAT services created in this router. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.auto_network_.text: Specifies the network tier for the NAT. Allowed values are FIXED_STANDARD, PREMIUM, STANDARD, and STANDARD_OVERRIDES_FIXED_STANDARD. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.drain_nat_ips.text: A list of external IP addresses to be drained from the NAT. These IPs will no longer be used for new connections but will continue to serve existing connections until they are closed. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.effective_tcp.text: The effective TCP TIME_WAIT timeout in seconds for Cloud NAT connections, reflecting the actual value in use (either the configured value or the default). Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.enable_dynami.text: If set to true, the NAT gateway dynamically allocates ports for each VM from a shared pool instead of using static port allocation. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.enable_endpoi.text: Whether to enable endpoint independent mapping for the NAT gateway. When enabled, the NAT gateway maps each internal IP and port pair to a unique external IP and port, independent of the destination. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.endpoint_type.text: The list of endpoint types supported by this NAT configuration, controlling which types of network endpoints can use the NAT. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.icmp_idle_tim.text: The idle timeout for ICMP connections in seconds. This controls how long an ICMP session is kept alive in the NAT without traffic before being closed. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.log_config.text: Configuration for NAT logging. This block allows enabling or disabling logging for the NAT gateway and specifying a filter to determine which connections are logged. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.log_config.en.text: Whether to enable logging for the NAT gateway. When set to true, logs are generated according to the filter specified in the log_config block. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.log_config.fi.text: Determines which NAT logs are exported. Valid values: ALL (log all NAT traffic), ERRORS_ONLY (log only failed translations), TRANSLATIONS_ONLY (log successful translations only). Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.max_ports_per.text: Maximum number of ports per VM used by the NAT configuration, per subnet. Defaults to 2048, with an allowed range of 64 to 65536. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.min_ports_per.text: The minimum number of ports allocated to each VM in the NAT configuration. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.name.text: The name of the Cloud NAT. This name must be unique within the parent router. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.nat64_subnetw.text: A list of subnetworks (self-links) to be used for NAT64. NAT64 enables IPv6-only resources to communicate with IPv4-only services by mapping IPv6 addresses to IPv4 addresses. Each listed subnetwork must be configured with an IPv6 address range. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The name of the subnetwork to use for NAT64. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.nat_ip_alloca.text: Specifies how NAT IP addresses are allocated. AUTO_ONLY automatically allocates NAT IPs; MANUAL_ONLY requires you to specify them in nat_ips. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.nat_ips.text: List of self-links of external IP addresses to be used for NAT. Only valid when nat_ip_allocate_option is set to MANUAL_ONLY; if empty, an automatically allocated IP is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.rules.text: A list of custom NAT rules. Each rule specifies a rule number, a match expression, and an action (e.g., translation or no translation) to control how traffic is routed through the NAT. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.rules.action.text: The action configuration for this NAT rule, defining how traffic matching the rule's match condition is NATed. It specifies the source NAT IPs (active and drain) to use. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.rules.action..text: The list of IP addresses to use as source NAT IPs for active connections when this NAT rule is applied. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

The list of source NAT IP ranges (in CIDR format) to use as the active NAT addresses for packets matching this rule. Required for the action block of a NAT rule. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

List of source NAT IP addresses to be drained. These IPs will not be used for new connections, but existing connections will continue to use them until they are removed or connections terminate. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
A list of source NAT IP ranges to be drained. These ranges are used to gracefully terminate existing connections during a migration or deactivation of NAT IPs. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.rules.descrip.text: A user-defined, human-readable description for the NAT rule. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.rules.match.text: An expression in Common Expression Language (CEL) that defines which traffic this NAT rule applies to. It can match on packet attributes like source or destination IP, protocol, and ports, e.g., `inIpRange(destination.ip, '203.0.113.0/24')`. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.rules.rule_nu.text: The unique number assigned to this NAT rule. Rules are evaluated in ascending order, and this number must be unique within the NAT configuration. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.source_subnet.text: Specifies which IP ranges of the subnets are eligible for NAT. Valid values are: ALL_SUBNETWORKS_ALL_IP_RANGES, ALL_SUBNETWORKS_ALL_PRIMARY_IP_RANGES, and LIST_OF_SUBNETWORKS. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

Controls which IPv6 subnetwork IP ranges are eligible for NAT64. Set to ALL_IPV6_SUBNETWORKS to use all IPv6 subnets in the region, or LIST_OF_IPV6_SUBNETWORKS to use only the specific subnets listed in the associated subnetwork configuration. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.subnetworks.text: The list of subnetworks that this NAT configuration applies to. Each object specifies a subnetwork and its NAT settings. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.subnetworks.n.text: The name of the subnetwork to include in the NAT configuration for this router NAT. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.subnetworks.s.text: List of the secondary ranges of the subnetwork that are allowed to use NAT. This can be provided only when 'LIST_OF_SECONDARY_IP_RANGES' is used for source_ip_ranges_to_nat. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

List of source IP ranges in the subnetwork that should be NATed. Valid values are 'ALL_IP_RANGES', 'PRIMARY_IP_RANGE', and 'LIST_OF_SECONDARY_IP_RANGES'. If 'LIST_OF_SECONDARY_IP_RANGES' is used, you must also specify `secondary_ip_range_names`. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.tcp_establish.text: Timeout in seconds for established TCP connections before they are considered idle and closed. Defaults to 1200 seconds. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.tcp_time_wait.text: Timeout for TCP connections in the TIME_WAIT state, specified in seconds, within the router's NAT configuration. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.tcp_transitor.text: The timeout in seconds for TCP transitory idle connections. A transitory connection is one that is in the process of being established (e.g., during the TCP handshake); if no traffic is seen within this timeout, the connection is dropped. Defaults to 30 seconds. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.type.text: The type of NAT configuration. Valid values are `PRIVATE` and `PUBLIC`. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.nats.udp_idle_time.text: The timeout (in seconds) for UDP connections through the NAT. Defaults to 30 seconds if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.ncc_gateway.text: URI of the ncc_gateway to which this router associated. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.network.text: URI of the network to which this router belongs. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.params.text: Additional router parameters. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.params.resource_ma.text: Tag keys/values directly bound to this resource. The field is allowed for INSERT only. The keys/values to set on the resource should be specified in either ID { : } or Namespaced format { : }. For example the following are valid inputs: * {"tagKeys/333" : "tagValues/444", "tagKeys/123" : "tagValues/456"} * {"123/environment" : "production", "345/abc" : "xyz"} Note: * Invalid combinations of ID & namespaced format is not supported. For instance: {"123/environment" : "tagValues/444"} is invalid. * Inconsistent format is not supported. For instance: {"tagKeys/333" : "tagValues/444", "123/env" : "prod"} is invalid. Optional.

google_compute_router.region.text: [Output Only] URI of the region where the router resides. You must specify this field as part of the HTTP request URL. It is not settable as a field in the request body. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_router.self_link.text: [Output Only] Server-defined URL for the resource. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_security_policy.adaptive_.text: Configuration options for Cloud Armor Adaptive Protection (CAAP). Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
Configuration options for L7 DDoS detection. This field is only supported in Global Security Policies of type CLOUD_ARMOR. Optional.
If set to true, enables CAAP for L7 DDoS detection. This field is only supported in Global Security Policies of type CLOUD_ARMOR. Optional.
Rule visibility can be one of the following: STANDARD - opaque rules. (default) PREMIUM - transparent rules. This field is only supported in Global Security Policies of type CLOUD_ARMOR. Optional.
Configuration options for layer7 adaptive protection for various customizable thresholds. Optional.
The minimum confidence score (between 0 and 1) that adaptive protection requires before automatically deploying mitigation rules for layer 7 DDoS defense.
The number of seconds that the auto-deploy system waits before automatically deploying the mitigation rules. If not set, the default value is 3600 seconds.

Specifies the traffic load threshold in requests per second that triggers automatic deployment of Layer 7 DDoS adaptive protection. When traffic exceeds this threshold and other conditions are met, Google Cloud Armor may automatically enable mitigation.
The absolute queries per second (QPS) threshold that triggers detection of a layer 7 DDoS attack.

The load threshold in requests per second that triggers detection of a potential DDoS attack by the layer 7 adaptive protection. Exceeding this threshold causes the system to start monitoring traffic for attack indicators.
Detection threshold in queries per second (QPS) relative to the baseline traffic level for triggering adaptive protection. A value greater than 1 indicates a multiple of the baseline QPS.

A list of traffic granularity configurations for the threshold. Each configuration defines a traffic type (such as SOURCE_IP or USER_AGENT) and a value to specify the granularity of traffic to which the threshold applies.
If true, the threshold is applied to each unique value (e.g., each source IP) independently, instead of aggregating all traffic together.

The type of traffic granularity. Valid values are `HTTP_HEADER_HOST` (group traffic by the HTTP Host header), `HTTP_PATH` (group traffic by the HTTP request path), and `UNSPECIFIED_TYPE` (default, unspecified).

google_compute_security_policy.advanced_.text: A list of custom Content-Type header values to apply the JSON parsing. As per RFC 1341, a Content-Type header value has the following format: Content-Type := type "/" subtype *[";" parameter] When configuring a custom Content-Type header value, only the type/subtype needs to be specified, and the parameters should be excluded. Optional.

Controls the JSON payload parsing mode for the security policy. Possible values: DISABLED (no JSON parsing), STANDARD (standard JSON parsing), or STANDARD_WITH_GRAPHQL (standard JSON plus GraphQL parsing).
Specifies the log level for the security policy, controlling how much detail is logged. Valid values are NORMAL and VERBOSE.
The maximum request size chosen by the customer with Waf enabled. Values supported are "8KB", "16KB, "32KB", "48KB" and "64KB". Values are case insensitive. Optional.
An optional list of case-insensitive request header names to use for resolving the callers client IP address. Optional.

google_compute_security_policy.associati.text: A list of associations that belong to this policy. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The ID of the resource (e.g., backend service or target instance) to which the security policy is attached.
The display name of the security policy association. This is a user-defined name used to identify the association.

A list of project IDs or project numbers to exclude from this security policy association. This is used when the security policy is associated with a parent resource such as an organization or folder, to prevent the policy from applying to the specified projects.
The ID of the security policy that is being associated.

google_compute_security_policy.creation_.text: Output only. [Output Only] Creation timestamp inRFC3339 text format. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_security_policy.ddos_prot.text: Configuration for DDoS protection on the security policy, containing the protection class. This field is computed and output-only, so it cannot be set in configuration.

Configures the adaptive protection mode for DDoS attacks. Allowed values are DISABLED, ENABLED, PREVIEW, and UNSPECIFIED_ADAPTIVE_PROTECTION (the default, which uses the provider's unspecified behavior).

DDoS Protection for Network Load Balancers (and VMs with public IPs) builds DDoS mitigations that minimize collateral damage. It quantifies this as the fraction of a non-abuse baseline that's inadvertently blocked. Rules whose collateral damage exceeds ddosImpactedBaselineThreshold will not be deployed. Using a lower value will prioritize keeping collateral damage low, possibly at the cost of its effectiveness in rate limiting some or all of the attack. It should typically be unset, so Advanced DDoS (and Adaptive Protection) uses the best mitigation it can find. Setting the threshold is advised if there are logs for false positive detections with high collateral damage, and will cause Advanced DDoS to attempt to find a less aggressive rule that satisfies the constraint. If a suitable rule cannot be found, the system falls back to either no mitigation for smaller attacks or broader network throttles for larger ones. Optional.
Specifies the Google Cloud Armor DDoS protection tier for this security policy. Valid values are ADVANCED, ADVANCED_PREVIEW, and STANDARD.

google_compute_security_policy.descripti.text: An optional description of this resource. Provide this property when you create the resource. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_security_policy.fingerpri.text: Specifies a fingerprint for this resource, which is essentially a hash of the metadata's contents and used for optimistic locking. The fingerprint is initially generated by Compute Engine and changes after every request to modify or update metadata. You must always provide an up-to-date fingerprint hash in order to update or change metadata, otherwise the request will fail with error412 conditionNotMet. To see the latest fingerprint, make get() request to the security policy. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_security_policy.id.text: Output only. [Output Only] The unique identifier for the resource. This identifier is defined by the server. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_security_policy.kind.text: Output only. [Output only] Type of the resource. Alwayscompute#securityPolicyfor security policies Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_security_policy.label_fin.text: A fingerprint for the labels being applied to this security policy, which is essentially a hash of the labels set used for optimistic locking. The fingerprint is initially generated by Compute Engine and changes after every request to modify or update labels. You must always provide an up-to-date fingerprint hash in order to update or change labels. To see the latest fingerprint, make get() request to the security policy. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_security_policy.labels.text: Labels for this resource. These can only be added or modified by thesetLabels method. Each label key/value pair must comply withRFC1035. Label values may be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_security_policy.name.text: Name of the resource. Provided by the client when the resource is created. The name must be 1-63 characters long, and comply withRFC1035. Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters long and match the regular expression `[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?` which means the first character must be a lowercase letter, and all following characters must be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit, except the last character, which cannot be a dash. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_security_policy.parent.text: Output only. [Output Only] The parent of the security policy. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_security_policy.recaptcha.text: Configuration for reCAPTCHA options in the security policy. This field is computed, meaning it is populated by the API and cannot be set manually.

An optional field to supply a reCAPTCHA site key to be used for all the rules using the redirect action with the type of GOOGLE_RECAPTCHA under the security policy. The specified site key needs to be created from the reCAPTCHA API. The user is responsible for the validity of the specified site key. If not specified, a Google-managed site key is used. This field is only supported in Global Security Policies of type CLOUD_ARMOR. Optional.

google_compute_security_policy.region.text: Output only. [Output Only] URL of the region where the regional security policy resides. This field is not applicable to global security policies. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_security_policy.rules.text: A list of rules that belong to this policy. There must always be a default rule which is a rule with priority 2147483647 and match all condition (for the match condition this means match "*" for srcIpRanges and for the networkMatch condition every field must be either match "*" or not set). If no rules are provided when creating a security policy, a default rule with action "allow" will be added. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_security_policy.rules.act.text: The action to take when a request matches the rule.

google_compute_security_policy.rules.hea.text: The header_action block configures the request headers to add or remove for requests that match this security policy rule.
A list of request headers to be added to matching requests. Each object specifies a header name and its value.
The name of the header to add to the request. For example, 'X-Frame-Options'.
The value of the request header to add. This is the literal string value that will be sent with the header.

google_compute_security_policy.rules.kin.text: The type of the resource. Always 'compute#securityPolicyRule'.

google_compute_security_policy.rules.mat.text: The match block configures the request criteria that trigger the rule. It can contain either a config block for source IP ranges or an expr block for a CEL expression, depending on the policy version.
The match configuration for the rule, which defines the traffic to match using parameters such as source IP ranges, versioned expression, and layer 4 configs.
List of source IP address ranges (in CIDR notation) that the rule uses to match traffic.
The expr block defines a match expression in Common Expression Language (CEL) that is evaluated against incoming requests. If the expression evaluates to true, the rule is applied.
A human-readable description of the expression, used to document the purpose or intent of the match condition.
The CEL expression that defines the match condition for the security policy rule. This expression is evaluated against incoming requests to determine if the rule applies.
Optional string that identifies the source location (e.g., file and line) of the CEL expression, used for error reporting and debugging.
The title for the match expression, providing a human-readable name to identify the expression in the security policy rule.
A list of site keys to be used for validating reCAPTCHA action tokens.
Specifies a list of reCAPTCHA site keys used to verify session tokens for this rule.
The version of the expression to use for the match rule. Currently, only 'SRC_IPS_V1' is supported, which matches on source IP addresses.

google_compute_security_policy.rules.net.text: Defines the network match criteria for a security policy rule, specifying conditions such as source and destination IP ranges, IP protocols, and ports that determine when the rule applies.

List of destination IP ranges (in CIDR format) that this network match rule applies to. Each entry can be an IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR block, e.g., '192.0.2.0/24' or '2001:db8::/32'. Traffic whose destination IP falls within any of these ranges will match the rule.
An optional list of destination ports to match. Each element may be a single port number (e.g., '80') or a range of ports (e.g., '80-90'). If not specified, all destination ports are matched.
A list of IP protocols that the rule matches. Traffic must use one of the specified protocols to match the rule; if omitted, the rule matches all IP protocols.
List of source Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) that the source IP address of the request must belong to for the rule to match.
A list of source IP address ranges in CIDR notation that incoming traffic must match for the rule to apply.
A list of source ports or port ranges (e.g., '80' or '80-90') to match in the network rule.
List of source region codes (two-letter ISO 3166 alpha-2 country codes) used to match requests based on the geographic location of the source IP address.
A list of user-defined fields for matching network traffic. Each object contains a field name and optional values to match against.
Identifies the user-defined field to match in network traffic.
A list of string values to match against the referenced user-defined field. The rule matches when the field value is equal to one of these values.

google_compute_security_policy.rules.pre.text: Configuration block for preconfigured WAF (Web Application Firewall) rules. This block contains exclusions that allow selectively disabling specific preconfigured WAF rules or parts of them for this security policy rule.
A list of exclusions for the preconfigured WAF configuration. Each exclusion defines rules or rule sets that are excluded from the managed preconfigured WAF rules.
A list of request cookies to exclude from the preconfigured WAF rule evaluation. Each object defines a cookie to be ignored when the rule inspects incoming requests.
The match operator to use for the cookie, such as CONTAINS, ENDS_WITH, EQUALS, EQUALS_ANY, or STARTS_WITH.
The value of the request cookie to exclude.
Specifies a list of request headers to exclude from the preconfigured WAF rule evaluation. When configured, these headers are not inspected by the WAF rules, helping to avoid false positives.
The operator used to match the request header value for exclusion from the preconfigured WAF rules. Valid values are CONTAINS, ENDS_WITH, EQUALS, EQUALS_ANY, and STARTS_WITH.
The value of the request header to exclude from the preconfigured WAF rule.
A list of request query parameters to exclude from evaluation by the preconfigured WAF rule. Each object defines a query parameter that should be ignored when the rule is applied.
The operator used to match the request query parameter name to exclude. Allowed values are: CONTAINS, ENDS_WITH, EQUALS, EQUALS_ANY, STARTS_WITH.

The value of the query parameter to be excluded. This is used together with the key to specify a particular query parameter and value that should be excluded from evaluation by the preconfigured WAF rules.

A list of request URIs to exclude from matching the preconfigured WAF rule. Each item defines a specific URI that should be excluded from evaluation, so requests to these URIs will not be blocked or flagged by this rule.
The operator used to match the request URI to exclude. Valid values are CONTAINS, ENDS_WITH, EQUALS, EQUALS_ANY, and STARTS_WITH.
A request URI to exclude from the preconfigured WAF rule's evaluation.
The list of specific rule IDs to exclude from the preconfigured WAF configuration. These are the target rules that the exclusion applies to.
The name of the predefined WAF rule set that this exclusion applies to.
If true, the rule is in preview mode, meaning the action is not enforced but traffic is logged for testing.

google_compute_security_policy.rules.pri.text: The priority of this rule. Rules are evaluated in order from lowest to highest value (i.e., lower numbers have higher precedence). The priority must be an integer between 0 and 2147483647.

google_compute_security_policy.rules.rat.text: This block configures the rate limiting behavior for the rule, including parameters like the threshold and enforcement key.
The duration in seconds that a client is banned when the rule action is 'rate_based_ban'.
The threshold that triggers a temporary ban for an IP address that has exceeded the rate limit. It includes a count of requests and an interval in seconds over which the count is measured.
The number of requests that must be exceeded to trigger the ban threshold.

The time interval in seconds during which the number of requests (count) is evaluated to determine if the ban threshold is exceeded. For example, an interval_sec of 60 means the count must be exceeded within a 60-second rolling window.
Action to take for requests that are within the configured rate limit (i.e., do not exceed the threshold).
The key type on which the rate limit is enforced. Valid values are ALL, ASN, HTTP_COOKIE, HTTP_HEADER, HTTP_PATH, IP, REGION_CODE, SNI, TLS_JA3_FINGERPRINT, TLS_JA4_FINGERPRINT, USER_IP, and XFF_IP.

A list of configurations that specify the keys on which to enforce the rate limit. Each configuration includes a key type (e.g., IP, HTTP_HEADER, HTTP_COOKIE) and can optionally define exclusions for the rate limit.
The name of the key to enforce rate limiting on, such as the header name or cookie name, as specified by the corresponding enforce_on_key_type field.

The type of request key to enforce rate limiting on. Valid values include: ALL, ASN, HTTP_COOKIE, HTTP_HEADER, HTTP_PATH, IP, REGION_CODE, SNI, TLS_JA3_FINGERPRINT, TLS_JA4_FINGERPRINT, USER_IP, XFF_IP.
The name of the key to enforce the rate limit on, used when the enforceOnKey field requires a key name (e.g., the HTTP header name when enforceOnKey is HTTP_HEADER).
Action to take when the rate limit threshold is exceeded. Valid values are 'deny(403)' and 'rateBasedBan'.
Options for the redirect action taken when requests exceed the rate limit threshold. Used when the exceed action is set to redirect, specifying the redirect type and target URL.
The target URL to redirect to when the rate limit is exceeded. Required when the redirect type is EXTERNAL_302.
The type of redirect to use when the rate limit is exceeded. Possible values are EXTERNAL_302, which redirects to an external URL, and GOOGLE_RECAPTCHA, which presents a Google reCAPTCHA challenge.
An object defining the request threshold that triggers rate limiting. It specifies the number of requests (count) allowed within a given time interval (interval_sec).
The number of requests allowed within the configured interval before the rate limit action is applied.
The time interval in seconds over which the rate limit count is measured. The rate limit is triggered when the number of requests within this interval reaches the specified count.

google_compute_security_policy.rules.red.text: Configuration for the redirect action to take when this rule matches. Contains settings such as redirect type and target.
The URL to redirect the request to when the redirect type is set to EXTERNAL_302. It specifies the destination for the redirect action.
The type of redirect action. Valid values are EXTERNAL_302, which redirects to an external URL with HTTP 302, and GOOGLE_RECAPTCHA, which redirects to Google reCAPTCHA.

google_compute_security_policy.self_link.text: Output only. [Output Only] Server-defined URL for the resource. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_security_policy.short_nam.text: User-provided name of the organization security policy. The name should be unique in the organization in which the security policy is created. This should only be used when SecurityPolicyType is CLOUD_ARMOR. The name must be 1-63 characters long, and comply with https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc1035.txt. Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters long and match the regular expression `[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?` which means the first character must be a lowercase letter, and all following characters must be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit, except the last character, which cannot be a dash. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_security_policy.type.text: The type indicates the intended use of the security policy. - CLOUD_ARMOR: Cloud Armor backend security policies can be configured to filter incoming HTTP requests targeting backend services. They filter requests before they hit the origin servers. - CLOUD_ARMOR_EDGE: Cloud Armor edge security policies can be configured to filter incoming HTTP requests targeting backend services (including Cloud CDN-enabled) as well as backend buckets (Cloud Storage). They filter requests before the request is served from Google's cache. - CLOUD_ARMOR_INTERNAL_SERVICE (preview only): Cloud Armor internal service policies can be configured to filter HTTP requests targeting services managed by Traffic Director in a service mesh. They filter requests before the request is served from the application. - CLOUD_ARMOR_NETWORK: Cloud Armor network policies can be configured to filter packets targeting network load balancing resources such as backend services, target pools, target instances, and instances with external IPs. They filter requests before the request is served from the application. This field can be set only at resource creation time. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_security_policy.user_defi.text: Definitions of user-defined fields for CLOUD_ARMOR_NETWORK policies. A user-defined field consists of up to 4 bytes extracted from a fixed offset in the packet, relative to the IPv4, IPv6, TCP, or UDP header, with an optional mask to select certain bits. Rules may then specify matching values for these fields. Example: userDefinedFields: - name: "ipv4_fragment_offset" base: IPV4 offset: 6 size: 2 mask: "0x1fff" Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The base protocol or address family on which this user-defined field operates. Valid values are IPV4, IPV6, TCP, and UDP.
The mask that identifies the field to extract from the request or response, such as an HTTP header name when base is 'request'.
The byte offset from the start of the selected base (e.g., TCP header) where the user-defined field begins. Offsets are zero-based; an offset of 0 refers to the first byte.

Specifies the fixed length in bytes to extract from the base (e.g., TCP or UDP header) when defining a user-defined field by size. This is mutually exclusive with 'match' and is used to capture a fixed-size portion of the packet.

google_compute_service_attachment.connec.text: Output only. [Output Only] An array of connections for all the consumers connected to this service attachment. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The URL of the consumer network that is connected to this service attachment, e.g. projects/{project}/global/networks/{network}. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The URL of the consumer endpoint (for example, a forwarding rule) that is connected to the service attachment. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The list of NAT IP addresses allocated for the consumer endpoint. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The number of connections that have been propagated to the consumer network from the producer network for this connected endpoint. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The unique identifier for the Private Service Connect connection associated with this connected endpoint. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The current status of the connected endpoint. Possible values are: ACCEPTED, CLOSED, NEEDS_ATTENTION, PENDING, REJECTED, and STATUS_UNSPECIFIED. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

The connection preference of service attachment. The value can be set to ACCEPT_AUTOMATIC. An ACCEPT_AUTOMATIC service attachment is one that always accepts the connection from consumer forwarding rules. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_service_attachment.consum.text: Specifies which consumer projects or networks are allowed to connect to the service attachment. Each project or network has a connection limit. A given service attachment can manage connections at either the project or network level. Therefore, both the accept and reject lists for a given service attachment must contain either only projects or only networks or only endpoints. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The maximum number of connections allowed for the consumer in the accept list. A value of 0 means no limit. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.
The URL of the network that is allowed to connect to this service attachment. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

The project ID or project number of a consumer project that is allowed to connect to the service attachment. Used in the consumer accept list to identify the allowed project. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

Specifies a list of projects or networks that are not allowed to connect to this service attachment. The project can be specified using its project ID or project number and the network can be specified using its URL. A given service attachment can manage connections at either the project or network level. Therefore, both the reject and accept lists for a given service attachment must contain either only projects or only networks. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_service_attachment.creati.text: Output only. [Output Only] Creation timestamp inRFC3339 text format. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_service_attachment.descri.text: An optional description of this resource. Provide this property when you create the resource. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_service_attachment.domain.text: If specified, the domain name will be used during the integration between the PSC connected endpoints and the Cloud DNS. For example, this is a valid domain name: "p.mycompany.com.". Current max number of domain names supported is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_service_attachment.enable.text: If true, enable the proxy protocol which is for supplying client TCP/IP address data in TCP connections that traverse proxies on their way to destination servers. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

This field will be ignored when inserting a ServiceAttachment. An up-to-date fingerprint must be provided in order to patch/update the ServiceAttachment; otherwise, the request will fail with error 412 conditionNotMet. To see the latest fingerprint, make a get() request to retrieve the ServiceAttachment. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_service_attachment.metada.text: Metadata of the service attachment. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_service_attachment.name.text: Name of the resource. Provided by the client when the resource is created. The name must be 1-63 characters long, and comply withRFC1035. Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters long and match the regular expression `[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?` which means the first character must be a lowercase letter, and all following characters must be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit, except the last character, which cannot be a dash. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_service_attachment.nat_ip.text: The number of NAT IP addresses to be allocated per connected endpoint. If not specified, the default value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_service_attachment.nat_su.text: An array of URLs where each entry is the URL of a subnet provided by the service producer to use for NAT in this service attachment. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_service_attachment.produc.text: The URL of a forwarding rule with loadBalancingScheme INTERNAL* that is serving the endpoint identified by this service attachment. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_service_attachment.propag.text: The number of consumer spokes that connected Private Service Connect endpoints can be propagated to through Network Connectivity Center. This limit lets the service producer limit how many propagated Private Service Connect connections can be established to this service attachment from a single consumer. If the connection preference of the service attachment is ACCEPT_MANUAL, the limit applies to each project or network that is listed in the consumer accept list. If the connection preference of the service attachment is ACCEPT_AUTOMATIC, the limit applies to each project that contains a connected endpoint. If unspecified, the default propagated connection limit is 250. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_service_attachment.psc_se.text: The lower 32 bits of the 64-bit PSC service attachment ID, represented as a decimal string. Optional.

google_compute_service_attachment.reconc.text: This flag determines whether a consumer accept/reject list change can reconcile the statuses of existing ACCEPTED or REJECTED PSC endpoints. - If false, connection policy update will only affect existing PENDING PSC endpoints. Existing ACCEPTED/REJECTED endpoints will remain untouched regardless how the connection policy is modified . - If true, update will affect both PENDING and ACCEPTED/REJECTED PSC endpoints. For example, an ACCEPTED PSC endpoint will be moved to REJECTED if its project is added to the reject list. For newly created service attachment, this boolean defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_service_attachment.region.text: Output only. [Output Only] URL of the region where the service attachment resides. This field applies only to the region resource. You must specify this field as part of the HTTP request URL. It is not settable as a field in the request body. Optional; if omitted, computed by GCP.

google_compute_target_https_proxy.tls_ea.text: Specifies whether TLS 1.3 0-RTT Data ("Early Data") should be accepted for this service. Early Data allows a TLS resumption handshake to include the initial application payload (a HTTP request) alongside the handshake, reducing the effective round trips to "zero". This applies to TLS 1.3 connections over TCP (HTTP/2) as well as over UDP (QUIC/h3). This can improve application performance, especially on networks where interruptions may be common, such as on mobile. Requests with Early Data will have the "Early-Data" HTTP header set on the request, with a value of "1", to allow the backend to determine whether Early Data was included. Note: TLS Early Data may allow requests to be replayed, as the data is sent to the backend before the handshake has fully completed.
